title: Span and Linear Dependence
topic: Span and linear dependence — two arrows fill a parallelogram (their span); a third coplanar arrow is dependent and adds nothing; an off-plane arrow lifts the span into all of R³, which is linear independence.

beats.narration: How much space do a few arrows give you?
Two arrows, v one and v two. Every combination of them — every a v one plus b v two — fills this whole parallelogram. We call that the span.

elements.content: Parallelogram fills with amber + dashed completion edges
'span(v₁, v₂) = { a v₁ + b v₂ }' on right panel

beats.narration: Now drop in a third arrow that lies flat inside the parallelogram. It's just a combination of the first two — linearly dependent. The span doesn't grow at all.

elements.content: Decomposition guides showing v₃ = c₁ v₁ + c₂ v₂

beats.narration: But swap in an arrow that lifts off the plane. Suddenly the span isn't a patch anymore — it fills the whole three dimensional space. That's linear independence.

elements.content: Switch to oblique-projection axes (x right, z back/up-right, y up). Floor parallelogram (v₁, v₂) tilts into perspective.
v₃ rises vertically out of plane (rose → amber-300 emphasis)
Parallelepiped wireframe emerges from sweep of floor along v₃

beats.narration: Span is your reach. Dependent vectors don't add to it. Independent ones do.

elements.content: 'Span is your reach.' — huge serif italic
